clue.text: Given cards so dealt Fred one

indicators.note: cards that are dealt are shuffled and handed out, so these letters are mixed up

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A card game: Fred is dealt his hand and plays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Given cards' looks like the card game of the surface, but to be given your cards is to be sacked. 'dealt' mixes FRED and I.
explanation.definitionFit: To get one's cards is a British idiom for being dismissed from a job, as an employer hands back the paperwork.

clue.text: Anyone like Charon was the last to have a row with

definitions.text: Anyone like Charon was the last to have a row with

parts.words: Anyone like Charon was the last to have a row with
parts.note: Charon rows the dead across the Styx, so he is the final person anyone takes a boat trip with

explanation.surface: Charon is the last person anyone would quarrel with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' reads as a quarrel; it is rowing a boat. Charon, in Greek myth, ferries the souls of the dead across the river Styx.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who rows passengers across a river for a fare, as Charon does for the dead.

clue.text: A stocktaker moving with whispers

explanation.surface: A warehouse clerk shuffles about, murmuring.
explanation.definitionFit: A cattle thief takes livestock; and something that makes soft crackling sounds as it moves, like dry leaves.

clue.text: Though it may lose or gain you a day it should show the corresponding time

definitions.text: Though it may lose or gain you a day it should show the corresponding time

parts.words: Though it may lose or gain you a day it should show the corresponding time
parts.note: crossing the imaginary meridian in the Pacific moves the calendar a day

explanation.surface: A faulty clock that runs fast or slow should still be right.
explanation.walkthrough: It sounds like a clock; it is the International Date Line in the Pacific, and a newspaper report's heading giving the place and date of a dispatch.
explanation.definitionFit: The meridian where the calendar date changes by one day; or a line atop a news story stating when it was written.

clue.text: Seized and formally tied up

explanation.surface: Someone is arrested and handcuffed in proper fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: A policeman who grabs a suspect has seized him; someone wearing a stiff collar and tie is dressed formally.

clue.text: Where one's figure does one no credit

definitions.text: Where one's figure does one no credit

parts.words: Where one's figure does one no credit
parts.note: in book-keeping a sum entered in the debts column is the opposite of a credit

explanation.surface: Someone whose physique is unflattering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'figure' suggests a body shape; it is a number in an account, and 'credit' is the accounting column too. The phrase also means 'as a disadvantage'.
explanation.definitionFit: The column of a ledger recording money owed or spent, the opposite of what is received.

clue.text: See 3
A cover-up of some vital statistics

definitions.text: A cover-up of some vital statistics

parts.words: A cover-up of some vital statistics
parts.note: vital statistics are a woman's bust, waist and hip measurements, and clothing covers them

explanation.surface: An official hides some embarrassing figures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cover-up' and 'statistics' suggest a scandal over figures; it is clothes covering a body's measurements.
explanation.definitionFit: An old literary word for clothing or apparel, which covers the body.

clue.text: Composition written with lamentable slowness

parts.note: a mournful piece of music, played slowly as a lament

explanation.surface: A writer took a shamefully long time over an essay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lamentable slowness' sounds like a slow writer; it describes the music's mournful slow tempo.
explanation.definitionFit: A funeral song or lament, typically slow and sorrowful.

clue.text: Me? I'm wrapped in contemplation

parts.note: someone thinking only about 'me' is preoccupied with their own person

explanation.surface: Someone asked a question is lost in thought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrapped in contemplation' reads as deep thought; the stress on 'Me' shows the thinker's subject is themself.
explanation.definitionFit: Preoccupation with one's own feelings and interests to the exclusion of others.

clue.text: A favour obtained by winning ways

definitions.text: A favour obtained by winning ways

parts.words: A favour obtained by winning ways
parts.note: a favour is a ribbon badge, and this one is won by coming first at a show

explanation.surface: Someone charms their way into getting a kindness.
explanation.definitionFit: A ribbon knot awarded to a prize-winner at a show is a favour earned by winning.

clue.text: Here Moroccans come home with greater zest

explanation.surface: Moroccans return home with renewed enthusiasm.
explanation.definitionFit: A port city in northern Morocco; and the comparative of tangy, sharper in flavour.

clue.text: A university ditty coming back to me finally

indicators.note: coming back means the word for the song is read in reverse order

parts.note: a lay is a short song or ballad

indicators.note: finally picks out the last letter of the word me

explanation.surface: A college song returns to the singer's mind at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming back' turns LAY into YAL; 'finally' takes the E ending 'me'.
explanation.definitionFit: An Ivy League institution in New Haven, Connecticut.

clue.text: Imitation post

explanation.surface: A fake mail delivery, two words in a row.
explanation.definitionFit: A painting 'in the manner of' an artist is an imitation; post as a prefix means later in time.

clue.text: Slightly depressed area in need of stirring up

indicators.note: stirring up a mixture jumbles it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A district a little down on its luck needs a shake-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stirring up' rearranges NEED. 'depressed' suggests gloom, but the area is physically low.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooded valley, a hollow in the land, is a mild dip below the surrounding ground.

clue.text: Bow to put off

explanation.surface: Someone bows and then postpones.
explanation.definitionFit: To yield to another's judgement; and to postpone until later.

clue.text: A draught of breathtaking efficacy!

parts.note: breathtaking is read literally: the drink stops one breathing for good

explanation.surface: A tonic so effective it leaves you gasping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breathtaking' reads as amazing; here the draught takes the drinker's breath away permanently.
explanation.definitionFit: A quantity of drug or poison large enough to kill.

clue.text: He'll go along with you for a pleasant get-together

explanation.surface: A friendly guest will accompany you to a nice social gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: An obliging person who consents is a willing participant; a nice social do is an enjoyable celebration.

clue.text: The forebear of an excitable coster

indicators.note: an excitable thing is jumpy and agitated, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A Victorian fruit seller's great-grandfather had a temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excitable' rearranges AN and COSTER. A coster (costermonger) is a London street seller of fruit and vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: A forefather, someone from whom one is descended.

clue.text: Putting pupils into different classes, for example

definitions.text: Putting pupils into different classes, for example

parts.words: Putting pupils into different classes, for example
parts.note: sorting schoolchildren into forms is one instance of grouping things by kind

explanation.surface: A school timetable sorts children into their forms.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about school streaming, but 'classes' means any categories.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorting things into kinds or groups is the general act of which streaming schoolchildren is one example.

clue.text: Where citizens may take aim with care, constitutionally

definitions.text: Where citizens may take aim with care, constitutionally

indicators.note: constitution is make-up, so the letters are made up anew in a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A country whose constitution lets citizens bear arms, if they shoot carefully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'constitutionally' rearranges AIM and CARE, and alludes to the US Second Amendment right to bear arms.
explanation.definitionFit: The United States, whose founding charter guarantees a right to bear arms.

clue.text: Practical knowledge within the viewer's range

explanation.surface: An expert's know-how lies within view.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep understanding of a situation; and, split in two, visible to someone looking.

clue.text: Strip off on the Manx shore

explanation.surface: Someone undresses on a beach on the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: To remove a rind or skin; and a town on the west coast of the Isle of Man, the island between Britain and Ireland.

clue.text: Religious resting-place for a little loopy embroidery

parts.note: pi is slang for pious, religious
a cot is a small bed for sleeping

explanation.surface: A church bed is decorated with lace loops.
explanation.walkthrough: PI, short for pious, is a crossword favourite for 'religious'; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A small loop of twisted thread forming an ornamental edging on lace or ribbon.

clue.text: Aphis in imitative style

indicators.note: a new style is a new fashioning, so the letters are reworked into a different order

explanation.surface: A greenfly copies something else's fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'style' rearranges APHIS, the greenfly. 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Behaving like an ape means copying others, mimicking them foolishly.

clue.text: An English rebel hanged in a basket

indicators.note: hanged in says the name hangs suspended inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A rebel was executed in a basket.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Aske led the Pilgrimage of Grace against Henry VIII in 1536 and was hanged in chains at York; 'hanged in' places his name inside 'a basket'.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Aske was a Yorkshire lawyer who led a Tudor rising and was executed for it.

clue.text: Nail turning blue-colour

indicators.note: turning the letters round about puts them in a new order

explanation.surface: A fingernail turns blue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' rearranges NAIL; the surface suggests a bruised fingernail.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigo dye or the shrub yielding it, a deep shade of blue.

clue.text: See 16
I make a song about one wine from Tuscany .

indicators.note: about means the word for singing surrounds the number one

parts.note: to chant is to sing a song
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone sings the praises of a Tuscan wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts I inside CHANT to give CHIANT; the clue's opening I goes at the end. 'make a song about' reads as fuss, but the words split.
explanation.definitionFit: A red wine named after the hills between Florence and Siena in central Italy.

clue.text: … though there's naturally nothing to drink during this

definitions.text: though there's naturally nothing to drink during this

parts.words: though there's naturally nothing to drink during this
parts.note: continues the wine clue before it: in a long dry spell nature supplies no water

explanation.surface: A follow-on from the wine clue: there's nothing left to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins it to 27, so it seems to be about the wine running out; 'naturally' points to weather instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A long spell without rain, when rivers and reservoirs run dry.

clue.text: A guide for a streetcar that runs alongside the court

explanation.surface: A rail for a tram that passes beside the law courts.
explanation.definitionFit: The rails a tram runs along; and, in tennis, the pair of parallel lines down each side of the court.

clue.text: To entrance and take pos session

explanation.surface: To charm someone and take them over.
explanation.definitionFit: To go in at a doorway, read as en-trance; and in law, to go on to land as a means of claiming ownership.
